candidates.decision_relevance: The reviews repeatedly note that weekly returns and rebounds do not reveal whether weakness preceded or followed recovery. A timestamped hourly BTC and ETH price history would make the price-path sequence and drawdowns directly auditable.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly adversarial reviews W37–W42; daily director outputs describe mixed short-window returns but note missing granular W42 paths.
candidates.metric_name: BTC and ETH hourly reference prices
candidates.missing_history_problem: Weekly summaries and selected return windows do not preserve the full within-week path needed to compare deterioration, drawdown, and rebound timing.

candidates.decision_relevance: Breadth is repeatedly used to distinguish narrow rebounds from broad participation, but reported snapshots use changing point-in-time memberships and are often proxy-only. Historical constituent-level observations would allow comparable breadth series to be derived and audited.
candidates.evidence_reference: W41–W42 reviews cite missing quantitative breadth sequences; daily outputs flag changing membership hashes and incompatible proxy snapshots.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped constituent returns and universe membership for breadth observations
candidates.missing_history_problem: Snapshot counts from changing universes cannot establish whether participation broadened or narrowed over time.

candidates.decision_relevance: ETF flows are cited as evidence for and against deterioration, yet several reviews have only weekly totals or a single settled session. A per-session history would clarify timing, persistence, and asset-level divergence.
candidates.evidence_reference: W40–W42 reviews report weekly totals or note absent numerical totals and time-ordered flow observations; daily outputs repeatedly identify single-session or stale ETF context.
candidates.metric_name: Settled daily BTC and ETH ETF flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregated or isolated settled observations cannot show whether flows persisted, reversed, or aligned with the price and breadth sequence.

candidates.decision_relevance: Reviews cannot assess warning timing or post-warning outcomes because matured observations are not consistently linked to frozen warning timestamps. Linking existing frozen records to subsequent realized price paths would support descriptive, time-aligned evaluation without treating overlapping observations as independent.
candidates.evidence_reference: W39–W42 reviews report zero eligible prospective typed rows, unlinked matured outcomes, or unavailable candidate specifications and subsequent paths.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen warning timestamp–linked subsequent BTC and ETH return and drawdown paths
candidates.missing_history_problem: Unlinked cohort counts and medians cannot establish which outcomes followed which warnings or whether the observations were available ex ante.
